prompt:
You are completing a 3-panel pixel art comic strip.

The LAYOUT image already has the correct characters placed in Panels 1 & 2.
YOUR ONLY JOBS are:
  1. START WITH THE LAYOUT IMAGE AS YOUR CANVAS. Copy every pixel of Panels 1 & 2 of the LAYOUT image into your output image unchanged. Do not re-render, do not regenerate, do not stylize them — they are a 1:1 paste from the LAYOUT.
  2. ON TOP of those preserved pixels, ADD only:
     a. Speech bubbles with dialog text to Panels 1 & 2 (over the empty near-white #F8F9F2 background space, never over the bot pixels).
     b. Panel 3 with the punchline character and bubble.
     c. The banner (top bar) and footer (bottom bar) text.
  3. Keep the exact same total dimensions and panel heights as the LAYOUT image.

THE BOTS IN PANELS 1 & 2 ARE NOT YOURS TO DRAW. They already exist in the LAYOUT image — Panel 1 has its own pair of bots (left + right) and Panel 2 has its own SEPARATE pair of bots (left + right) which may look entirely different from Panel 1's bots. Do NOT copy Panel 1's bots into Panel 2's slots. Do NOT copy Panel 2's bots into Panel 1's slots. Each panel keeps the EXACT pixel-perfect characters drawn in that specific panel of the LAYOUT — even if it means the bots in the two panels look completely different. The LAYOUT is your source of truth, panel by panel.

CHARACTER PIXEL LOCK (panels 1 & 2 — STRICTLY ENFORCED, ZERO TOLERANCE):
The characters in Panels 1 & 2 of the LAYOUT image are ALREADY DRAWN PIXEL-PERFECTLY. Your job is to PRESERVE THEM AS-IS — copy them out of the LAYOUT image at the pixel level into your output. Do NOT redraw. Do NOT regenerate. Do NOT "interpret" them. Do NOT substitute a generic-looking bot in their place.

Specifically for EVERY character in Panels 1 & 2:
- The entire character (body, head, face, eyes, mouth, ears, antennas, color, all visual details) MUST match the LAYOUT image EXACTLY pixel-for-pixel. Same poses, same shapes, same proportions, same colors. If you can spot any difference between your output character and the LAYOUT image character, you have failed.
- Each panel has its OWN distinct characters as drawn in the LAYOUT. The character in Panel 1 left slot may be DIFFERENT from the character in Panel 2 left slot. Do NOT reuse one bot's design across panels — copy each panel's character independently from the LAYOUT.
- The ONLY thing you may add on top of the characters is anti-aliased smoothing of existing outlines (without changing shape). You may NOT add features, you may NOT remove features, you may NOT recolor.

WHEN IN DOUBT: trace the LAYOUT image pixels. The LAYOUT character pixels are AUTHORITATIVE — your output must reproduce them faithfully.

EMPTY SLOTS — STRICT: If a character slot in Panel 1 or Panel 2 is EMPTY in the LAYOUT image (no character was placed there — just plain panel background), then leave that exact spot COMPLETELY EMPTY in your output: only the plain #F8F9F2 panel background, nothing else. Do NOT invent, add, hallucinate, duplicate, or imagine any bot/character/figure in an empty slot. An empty slot stays empty. Speech bubbles may still appear over that empty space, but no character.

PANEL SIZES — copy from LAYOUT image exactly. Heights are fixed. Panel 3 is intentionally shorter. Do not expand it.

BACKGROUND — FIXED, NON-NEGOTIABLE: The panel background color is ALWAYS EXACTLY #F8F9F2 — RGB (248, 249, 242), which is a VERY PALE, ALMOST-WHITE off-white (only a hair off pure white). It is NOT "sage", NOT green, NOT gray, NOT a medium or dark tone — it is essentially white with the faintest warm tint. EVERY panel (Panel 1, Panel 2, Panel 3) must have this IDENTICAL near-white #F8F9F2 background — all panels match exactly, zero variation. Do NOT darken it, do NOT make it gray/green/beige, do NOT tint, shade, gradient, or vary it. If your background comes out medium-toned, grayish, greenish, or dark, it is WRONG — it must look almost white. The bots, bubbles, banner, and footer keep their own colors and do not affect this.
BOT COLORS: The bots MUST keep their original colors exactly as in their reference images. The bot body and face background is WHITE — do NOT tint it with the panel background color. Only the panel area behind the bots changes color, not the bots themselves.

SPEECH BUBBLES — follow this exactly:
- Copy the tail style and font from the BUBBLE STYLE image, but make every bubble a ROUNDED rectangle (softly rounded corners), NOT square.
- BUBBLE EDGES: every speech bubble's outline/border and its rounded corners must be SMOOTH, clean and ANTI-ALIASED (non-pixelated) — no jagged or stair-stepped edges on the bubble shape. (The TEXT inside the bubbles still stays blocky pixel/bitmap font — only the bubble's own outline is smooth and rounded.)
- TWO BUBBLE STYLES based on speaker:
  * Left Bot bubbles: solid BLACK rounded rectangle, softly rounded corners, smooth anti-aliased edges, WHITE pixel text inside.
  * Right Bot bubbles: solid WHITE rounded rectangle, softly rounded corners, smooth anti-aliased edges, BLACK pixel text inside, with a thin smooth BLACK border (1-2px).
- Panel 3 bubble is ALWAYS black background with white text (it is the Left Bot's punchline).
- The color for each bubble is specified in the EXACT BUBBLE LAYOUT below — follow it per bubble.
- STACKING: When a panel has multiple bubbles, stack them top-to-bottom in the exact dialog order listed below. The first line of dialog = topmost bubble. The second = directly below it. No gaps between bubbles.
- FIRST BUBBLE PLACEMENT: The first bubble in Panels 1 & 2 must start at the very top of the panel (flush against the top border, with only 2–3px padding). It should be tall enough to fill the open space above the characters. Do not leave white space at the top of the panel.
- EACH bubble gets its own tail pointing to its speaker. Tails do not connect bubbles to each other.
- DIALOG ORDER IS SACRED — do not swap, skip, or reorder any lines.

FONT SIZE RULES FOR PANELS 1 & 2 (CRITICAL — maximize readability):
- The bubble area is the open space ABOVE the bots and BETWEEN the bots. Bubbles must fill this entire space.
- Calculate the available vertical space: the bubble zone has TWO sub-regions that bubbles can use together. (a) TOP REGION: from the top of the panel down to the top of the tallest character's head — full panel width. (b) MIDDLE-GAP REGION: the vertical strip BETWEEN the left and right bots, extending from the top of their heads all the way DOWN to the panel bottom — narrower than the top region but tall. A single bubble can span BOTH regions, taking a "shoulder" or "T" shape: wide at the top (filling region a), then narrowing as it continues downward into region b between the bots. This lets a LONG dialog claim a taller area and therefore support a bigger font. Use the T-shape ONLY when a single dialog is too long to fit on one or two WIDE lines in region (a); for short or medium dialog, keep the bubble WIDE and shallow in region (a) — one wide line when it fits. Do NOT force short text into a tall narrow shape just to fill region (b).
- Calculate the available horizontal space: the full panel width minus small margins (6px each side).
- Use the LARGEST font size that allows all dialog lines to fit within the bubble zone. The text should feel oversized and bold — never small or cramped.
- Each bubble should be as WIDE as the panel allows and as TALL as needed to fill the vertical space evenly.
- WIDTH FIRST — FEWEST LINES: Lay out every bubble's dialog on the FEWEST possible lines by widening the bubble. If a phrase fits across the available width at the big font, put it on ONE wide line (e.g. "SURE? HAVE YOU TRIED?" or "SORTA OF, GIVE IT A TRY" = ONE line each, never split into two narrow lines). Only break to a 2nd or 3rd line when the text genuinely will not fit one line at the target font. For the same text, ALWAYS prefer a WIDE, shorter bubble over a NARROW, taller one. Splitting a short phrase into multiple cramped lines is WRONG.
- If there are 2 bubbles in a panel, each gets roughly half the bubble zone height.
- MATCH THE BUBBLE-AND-FONT PROPORTIONS from the BUBBLE STYLE reference image — bubble size relative to panel, font size relative to bubble, font weight, font style. Look at ONLY those proportions in that image. DO NOT look at any bot, face, eye, mouth, antenna, or character feature in the BUBBLE STYLE image — those are NOT references for anything in your output. The characters in your output come EXCLUSIVELY from the LAYOUT image (panel by panel). If you find yourself drawing any character feature that resembles something from the BUBBLE STYLE image, STOP — those features are wrong; go back to the LAYOUT character pixels. Minimum font size: 32px. Target font size: 36-44px — chunky, readable from a distance. Bubbles must be GENEROUSLY sized — fill the bubble zone, do not be conservative or shy with bubble size.
- WHITE SPACE IS WASTED SPACE. If there is visible empty space above or between bubbles, increase the font size or bubble size until the space is filled.

  BUBBLE 3 (BELOW bubble 2): "BUT HUSBAND WANTS FOOTBALL" — speaker: Left Bot — BLACK background, WHITE text — place in the LEFT half of panel, tail points LEFT toward the left character.
  BUBBLE 4 (BELOW bubble 3): "ANY IDEAS?" — speaker: Left Bot — BLACK background, WHITE text — place in the LEFT half of panel, tail points LEFT toward the left character.

PANEL 2 — 4 bubbles in this order:

  BUBBLE 2 (BELOW bubble 1): "EXCUSE ME?!" — speaker: Left Bot — BLACK background, WHITE text — place in the LEFT half of panel, tail points LEFT toward the left character.
  BUBBLE 3 (BELOW bubble 2): "IT'S REALITY TV... FOR US!" — speaker: Right Bot — WHITE background, BLACK text — place in the RIGHT half of panel, tail points RIGHT toward the right character.
  BUBBLE 4 (BELOW bubble 3): "AND GET POPCORN, THIS WILL BE FUN" — speaker: Right Bot — WHITE background, BLACK text — place in the RIGHT half of panel, tail points RIGHT toward the right character.

PANEL 3 — 1 bubble in this order:
  BUBBLE 1 (TOP — first in the panel): "HOLY CHIP !!" — speaker: Left Bot — BLACK background, WHITE text — place in the LEFT half of panel, tail points LEFT toward the left character.

PANEL 3:
- Height is FIXED — copy from LAYOUT. It is short. Do NOT expand it.
- Show ONLY "Left Bot" on the LEFT side, bubble on the RIGHT.
- Draw the character at 130% of its natural size (30% larger than normal). Any part that goes outside Panel 3's borders must be hard-cropped — do not expand the panel to accommodate it.
- Character positioned 2px from its panel edge (left character: 2px from left border; right character: 2px from right border) and pressed against the panel bottom border. The center space is entirely reserved for the speech bubble.
- SPEECH BUBBLE in Panel 3: Draw it 2x larger than the bubbles in Panels 1 & 2 — bigger rectangle, bigger font. It must dominate the center space of Panel 3.
- Use the PANEL 3 SHAPE image for body proportions and colors only. Generate a NEW expression that directly reflects the story:
  1. Read the full dialog from all 3 panels carefully.
  2. Identify the emotional beat of Panel 3's line specifically — is it sarcasm, shock, joy, defeat, pride, confusion?
  3. Express THAT exact emotion on the character's face. The expression must make sense to someone reading the story. A viewer should look at the face and immediately understand the punchline.
  4. Amplify the emotion for comedic effect using the character's own feature shapes.
- IMAGE QUALITY IS CRITICAL: The character in Panel 3 must have IDENTICAL rendering quality to the characters already drawn in Panels 1 & 2 of the LAYOUT image. Match their exact line weight, fill quality, and level of detail. Do NOT downgrade resolution or introduce any pixelation, dithering, or noise.
- SHAPE RULE — strictly enforced: Every individual element of the character (eyes, mouth, pupils, cheeks, body parts, antennae tips, etc.) must be drawn as EITHER a perfect square OR a perfect circle. No other shapes allowed. No irregular polygons, no freehand curves, no jagged outlines. If it is not a perfect square, it must be a perfect circle. Solid flat fill, hard edge, zero anti-aliasing.
